name: Guadalupe Mountains National Park
blurb: Desert grass, canyon springs and the cougar that hunts mule deer.

tip.title: Skip the summer monsoon
tip.text: Most of the desert's rain falls in summer. Set Monsoon rain to -100% and watch the grasses, then seed-eaters like kangaroo rats and the snakes that hunt them.

sources.title: NPS: Guadalupe Mountains nature and science

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Guadalupe Mountains National Park, Chihuahuan Desert, Elk). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.name: Grama grasses
nodes.desc: Blue grama, black grama and relatives dominate the desert grasslands of the Chihuahuan Desert, the grass layer that seed-eaters and grazers rely on.
A shrub of rocky slopes and washes, among the most recorded plants near the park. GloBI records show mule deer eating it.
Grows with juniper on the lower eastern slopes. Its seeds are eaten by rock squirrels in GloBI records.
Grows in canyon bottoms such as McKittrick, where Wikipedia says the trees depend on spring water. Its acorns are food for squirrels and mice.
Cactus pads and fruit are abundant on desert slopes and uplands and give moisture and food to animals such as peccaries.
The best recorded large mammal near the park. It browses shrubs such as Apache plume and is a main prey of the cougar.
Listed among the large mammals of the park. Grasses are a year-round staple of elk diet, and cougars are among their predators.
A small desert rodent that mostly eats seeds, including grass seeds. Snakes and coyotes hunt it.
Eats seeds and nuts such as pinyon seeds, and is prey of cougars, rattlesnakes, bullsnakes and eagles.
One of many mice of the park. Eats seeds and insects, and is a common prey of snakes.
A seed- and fruit-eating bird of desert scrub. GloBI records show rattlesnakes and bullsnakes eating it.

nodes.name: Western diamond-backed rattlesnake
nodes.desc: Ambushes kangaroo rats, mice, squirrels and birds, according to GloBI records.
Scavenges carcasses of deer, peccary and squirrels, and so returns dead matter to the food web.
Listed among the park's carnivores. Eats rodents and also feeds on carrion.

nodes.name: Cougar
nodes.desc: The top predator. Mule deer are a main prey; GloBI records also show it taking peccary and rock squirrels, and elk are known prey.
A raptor of cliffs and open country in the park. Takes ground squirrels and other small animals.
Strong sun and heat drive desert plant growth and also dry the ground.
Most rain falls from late June to early October with the summer monsoon, in a desert averaging about 235 mm a year.
Thin limestone soils hold nutrients that plants take up.
Fungi, bacteria and insects break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil.

story: Guadalupe Mountains National Park in Texas has Guadalupe Peak, the highest point in the state at 8,751 feet. The trail to the summit climbs through pinyon pine and Douglas-fir forest above the Chihuahuan Desert. In McKittrick Canyon, springs feed bigtooth maple, velvet ash and chinkapin oak.
matters: Springs let deciduous trees grow in a desert range. People have lived in its caves and alcoves for over 10,000 years.
